Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Statistical Data Call Calendar for all 51 jurisdictions and every designated statistical agent (ISO/Verisk, NCCI, AIPSO, ISS, NISS); escalates at-risk entries to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Alabama statistical plan and the ALDOI statistical agent designation re-read at calendar build, plus the Arizona, California and Connecticut statistical plans; each state's current stat-plan edition and the agent's latest data reporting circular are cited on the calendar row

In-scope processes.value: Statistical data call intake and scheduling for Alternative Risk and all other lines — annual stat plan cycles, NCCI unit statistical and financial calls, ISO monthly/quarterly stat submissions, AIPSO residual market calls and one-off state special data calls in all 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Statistical Data Call Calendar register (one row per jurisdiction × agent × call), fed by agent circular subscriptions and state bulletin monitoring

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statistical Data Call Calendar Procedure — agent designation lookup per state/line, circular monitoring, due-date derivation, back-scheduled internal milestones, ad-hoc call intake within 5 business days

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually each January and on any state stat-plan amendment or agent circular that changes a due date

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per data call — NCCI unit statistical reports at 18 months from policy effective date plus the 20-day reporting window (then 1st–5th subsequent reports annually), NCCI policy data within 30 days of policy effective date, NCCI financial calls at March 31/April 1, ISO stat submissions monthly on the agent's published cycle, NAIC MCAS at April 30, and the stated response date on each state special call

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar alerts at T-60 (data owner mobilised), T-30 (extract due), T-10 (validation complete) and T-2 business days (submission due) against every statistical call row, routed to the named data owner and the Regulatory Reporting Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Each approved quarterly version of the Data Call Calendar, the circular/bulletin captures behind every due date and the ad-hoc call intake forms, retained 7 years from the reporting period

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any statistical call discovered after its due date, or absent from the calendar when it should have been scheduled, is raised as a calendar-completeness exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off each quarterly calendar version and every missed/late-discovered statistical call remediation before the exception is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All statistical calls with a due date in the quarter across the 51 jurisdictions, from the Data Call Calendar, plus an independently rebuilt obligation list from agent circulars and state bulletins for the same period

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on completeness — any obligation on the independent list absent from the calendar is a fail; any calendar row with a due date that does not match the agent circular is a fail; ≥1 fail escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per data call; the calendar completeness test runs quarterly over that quarter's due dates, with 100% coverage of NCCI and ISO recurring cycles and of all Alabama entries

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not maintain the Data Call Calendar or own any sampled call

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly Data Call Calendar completeness workpaper (independent obligation list, calendar extract, matching, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-007-C01

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Calendar extract by jurisdiction and agent with due date, statutory/stat-plan cite and submission status, producible for an ALDOI or NAIC market conduct data request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers agent (ISO/NCCI/AIPSO) data-reporting queries; Regulatory Affairs Manager owns direct state department inquiries and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of a missed statistical call

checklist.step: Stand up the master statistical reporting register for all 51 jurisdictions
actions: Open the Internal Regulatory System, go to Registers ▸ Statistical Reporting and create the current reporting-year register.
Ask Finance for the list of writing companies with their NAIC company codes and group code, and the states each is licensed in, and paste it in as the jurisdiction grid.
Create one row per jurisdiction × writing company × line of business (Alternative Risk, Property, Auto, Workers Compensation, Liability), 51 jurisdictions including DC.

Add the columns the calendar is judged on: designated statistical agent, stat plan name and edition, call name, reporting period, evaluation date, due date, source system, data owner, submission channel, status.
Mark Alabama as the representative jurisdiction row for REG-007 evidence sampling.
checklist.done: the register holds a row for every jurisdiction × company × line with no blank agent or stat-plan column.

checklist.step: Confirm the designated statistical agent for every state and line
actions: For each state row, open the department of insurance website and locate the statistical agent designation bulletin or the statistical plan order — for Alabama, the ALDOI bulletin designating the statistical agents for property/casualty experience.

Record the designated agent per line: NCCI for workers compensation in NCCI states, ISO/Verisk for property, general liability and commercial multi-peril, AIPSO for residual market automobile, ISS or NISS where the company has elected them.

Note the independent bureau states separately (for example California WCIRB for workers compensation, New York NYCIRB, Pennsylvania and Delaware PCRB) because their plans and due dates differ from NCCI.
Save the designation page as <state>-stat-agent-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf into the compliance evidence repository and link it on the register row.
Send the finished agent-by-state matrix to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for review.
checklist.done: every state × line row names a designated statistical agent backed by a dated department capture.

checklist.step: Verify the company is registered and entitled with each statistical agent
actions: For NCCI, sign in to ncci.com and open Data Manager ▸ Data Manager Dashboard; confirm each carrier code is listed and the Data Transfer entitlement is active for WCPOLS, WCSTAT and the financial calls.
For ISO/Verisk, sign in to the Verisk client portal and open Statistical Reporting ▸ Data Submission; confirm the company's ISO company number and the stat plans it is enrolled under.
For AIPSO, confirm the residual market reporting entitlement for each state plan the company services.
List any missing entitlement and email the agent's data reporting contact to have it opened, recording the request date and ticket reference on the register row.
Confirm at least two named users hold each entitlement so a single absence cannot block a submission.
checklist.done: every agent portal shows an active reporting entitlement for each carrier code, with at least two entitled users.

checklist.step: Subscribe to the circular and bulletin feeds that change due dates
actions: Subscribe the regulatory-reporting shared mailbox to NCCI Data Reporting circulars, ISO/Verisk statistical circulars and AIPSO bulletins, and to each state department's bulletin distribution list.

Create a mailbox rule that routes anything titled 'data call', 'statistical plan', 'unit statistical', 'financial call' or 'reporting requirement' into a Stat Reporting folder with a 2-business-day triage flag.
Post a Teams channel connector so new circulars appear in the Regulatory Reporting channel for the whole team, not one inbox.
Record on the register which feed each due date came from, so a changed circular can be traced to the rows it affects.
checklist.done: every agent and department feed is subscribed, routed and triaged within 2 business days, with feed-to-row traceability recorded.

checklist.step: Load the NCCI-driven workers compensation and Alternative Risk due dates
actions: Open the NCCI Statistical Plan and the current Data Reporting circular and list the recurring obligations: policy data (WCPOLS) within 30 days of policy effective date, unit statistical reports (WCSTAT) at 18 months from policy effective date reported within the 20-day window, subsequent reports annually to the 5th, and Detailed Claim Information on qualifying claims.

Add the annual financial calls: Policy Year Call for Compensation Experience, Calendar-Accident Year Call, Large Deductible Call and the Residual Market calls, with their March 31 / April 1 due dates.
For Alternative Risk business, add the large deductible and self-insured-group reporting rows separately — their exposure and premium fields differ from guaranteed cost.
For each row set the evaluation date (valuation date) as well as the due date, because the extract must be taken as of the valuation date, not the run date.
Enter the circular number and issue date in the citation column of every row you created.
checklist.done: every NCCI obligation has a register row with valuation date, due date and the circular number it came from.

checklist.step: Load the ISO/Verisk statistical plan submission cycles
actions: Open the Verisk statistical reporting site and download the current Commercial Statistical Plan, Personal Automobile Statistical Plan and Homeowners Statistical Plan editions the company reports under.
Read the submission schedule section and enter the monthly or quarterly transmission cycle with the agent's cut-off day for each plan.
Record the record types the plan requires (premium transaction records, loss transaction records, and any special call supplements) on the row.
Check the plan's edition date against the edition already coded in the extract mappings and raise a change request to the Data Management team where they differ.
Attach the plan cover page and schedule page to the register row as dated evidence.
checklist.done: each ISO stat plan has a register row showing edition, record types, cycle and cut-off day, with the plan pages attached.

checklist.step: Load AIPSO residual market and state-specific special calls
actions: List the states where the company services residual market automobile business and enter the AIPSO reporting cycle and due dates for each plan.

Search each department's bulletin archive for the past 24 months for recurring state-only calls — market share and premium calls, catastrophe/claims data calls, credit-based insurance score calls, and any Alternative Risk or captive supplements.
Enter each recurring state call with its response window as stated in the bulletin (commonly 30 or 45 days from issuance).
Flag calls answered outside the statistical agent — those go direct to the department portal and need their own credentials.
checklist.done: residual market and recurring state-only calls are on the register with their bulletin cite and response window.

checklist.step: Load NAIC-administered calls that ride alongside the statistical plans
actions: Check the NAIC Market Conduct Annual Statement participation list for each line and state to see which company/state/line combinations are required to file MCAS this year.
Enter the MCAS rows with the April 30 due date and the NAIC MCAS application in iSite+ as the submission channel.
Add any NAIC special data call the company is in scope for and record its stated due date and contact.
Cross-check that MCAS rows do not duplicate a statistical agent row for the same data — they are separate obligations with separate evidence.
checklist.done: every in-scope MCAS and NAIC special call is on the register with its April 30 or stated due date and channel.

checklist.step: Assign a data owner and a source system to every calendar row
actions: For each row name the accountable data owner by role — Policy Administration Analyst for premium and exposure, Claims Analyst for loss and claim detail, Premium Auditor for audited exposure, Reserving Analyst for case and bulk reserves.
Record the source system each field set comes from (policy administration platform, claims platform, premium audit, general ledger) on the row.
Where a required field has no system of record, log it as a data gap in the tracker with the owner and target date rather than leaving the cell blank.
Publish the owner assignment to the named owners and get their acknowledgement in writing.
checklist.done: every row has an acknowledged data owner, a named source system, and any missing field logged as a data gap.

checklist.step: Back-schedule internal milestones from each regulatory due date
actions: For each row compute extract date = due date minus 30 calendar days, validation-complete date = due date minus 10 business days, sign-off date = due date minus 5 business days, submit-by date = due date minus 2 business days.
Where the call has a valuation date (NCCI unit statistical at 18 months), set the extract date after the valuation date and never before it.
Where the source system closes monthly, align the extract date to the close calendar you get from the Controller so the extract sits on closed data.
Write all four milestone dates onto the register row and publish the resulting month-by-month workload view.
checklist.done: each row shows four computed internal milestones that sit after the valuation date and before the regulatory due date.

checklist.step: Configure reminders and the escalation ladder on every row
actions: In the Statistical Reporting register open Notifications and set alerts at T-60, T-30, T-10 and T-2 business days against the regulatory due date.
Route T-60 and T-30 to the named data owner, T-10 to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst, and T-2 to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Add an auto-escalation to the Head of Compliance for any row still in status 'Not started' at T-10.
Send yourself a test alert on one Alabama row and confirm it arrives at the right addresses before enabling the set.
checklist.done: alerts fire at T-60/T-30/T-10/T-2 to the correct recipients and the T-10 auto-escalation is proven by a test alert.

checklist.step: Run the monthly forward-horizon review with the data owners
actions: Hold a monthly 60-minute review covering every row with a due date in the next 90 days.
Walk each row's status against its four internal milestones and mark it Green / Amber / Red with a one-line reason.
Take from each data owner a committed extract date for Amber rows and record it on the row.
Minute the meeting, attach the minutes to the register, and re-issue the horizon view to the owners the same day.
checklist.done: every row due in 90 days carries a RAG status, a reason and a committed date, minuted and re-issued.

checklist.step: Intake ad-hoc and special data calls within 5 business days of receipt
actions: Triage the Stat Reporting mailbox folder daily; open an intake form for anything that requests company data with a response date.
Capture on the form: issuing department or agent, bulletin or circular number, lines and states in scope, data elements requested, valuation date, response date, submission channel and contact.
Decide applicability against the writing companies and lines, and record 'not applicable' calls with the reason rather than deleting them.
Create the register row for applicable calls within 5 business days of receipt and assign the data owner immediately.
Where the response window is under 30 days, notify the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day so resource is pulled forward.
checklist.done: every received call has a dated intake form and either a register row within 5 business days or a recorded not-applicable reason.

checklist.step: Escalate at-risk statistical calls before the due date passes
actions: Each week list rows that are Red or still 'Not started' inside T-10 business days.
For each, raise an escalation to the Head of Compliance and the data owner's manager within one business day, stating the jurisdiction, agent, call, due date and the specific blocker.
Present the options in writing: pull resource, request an extension from the agent or department in writing before the due date, or submit partial data with a documented cover note.
Where an extension is requested, record the agent/department contact, request date and the written response on the register row.
Record the decision and owner — silently missing the due date is never one of the options.
checklist.done: every at-risk row has a written escalation, a chosen option with an owner, and any extension evidenced in writing.

checklist.step: Version, approve and retain the quarterly calendar
actions: At each quarter end export the register to a versioned Data Call Calendar file named REG-007-calendar-<yyyy>Q<n>.
Attach the circular, bulletin and stat-plan captures that support the quarter's due dates.
Route the version to the Compliance Manager for sign-off and record the approval date and name in the file header.
File the approved version in the compliance evidence repository under REG-007-C01 with a 7-year retention label and confirm it is searchable by jurisdiction, agent and call name.
checklist.done: an approved, signed quarterly calendar version with its supporting captures is filed, labelled and searchable.

testing.step: Rebuild an independent obligation list for the quarter from primary sources
actions: Without opening the register, list the statistical obligations due in the quarter from the primary sources: NCCI Data Reporting circulars, the ISO/Verisk stat plan submission schedules, AIPSO bulletins, department bulletin archives for all 51 jurisdictions, and the NAIC MCAS participation list.
For each obligation record jurisdiction, writing company, line, agent, call name, valuation date and due date.
Note the source document number and date for every entry so the list is defensible.
testing.done: an independently sourced obligation list exists for the quarter with a source document cited on every entry.

testing.step: Extract the calendar population and reconcile it to the independent list
actions: Export from the Statistical Reporting register every row with a due date inside the quarter, across all writing companies and 51 jurisdictions.
Match register rows to the independent list on jurisdiction + company + line + call name.
List obligations present on the independent list but missing from the register as completeness exceptions, and register rows with no source obligation as over-scheduling observations.
Reconcile the counts and get the extractor to sign the extract as complete before sampling.
testing.done: the register and the independent list are reconciled item by item, with every unmatched entry listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Alabama rows and 100% of NCCI unit statistical and financial call rows.
Take 25 further rows at random using a recorded seed across the remaining jurisdictions, for a minimum of 40 rows.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and selection tool in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Ensure at least one ad-hoc state special call is in the sample.
testing.done: a reproducible sample of at least 40 rows is drawn, covering Alabama, NCCI cycles and one ad-hoc call.

testing.step: Re-perform the designated statistical agent determination for each sampled state
actions: For each sampled state open the department of insurance site and locate the current statistical agent designation or statistical plan order without looking at the register first.
Reach your own conclusion on the agent for that line — NCCI, ISO/Verisk, AIPSO, an independent bureau such as WCIRB or PCRB, or ISS/NISS.
Compare to the recorded agent; treat a right agent with a stale or missing citation as an exception in its own right.
Screenshot the designation page into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent agent conclusion, a comparison result and a captured source page.

testing.step: Recompute the due date and the internal milestone maths
actions: For NCCI unit statistical rows recompute due date = policy effective date + 18 months + the 20-day reporting window and compare to the register.

For NCCI financial call rows confirm the March 31 / April 1 date matches the current circular; for MCAS rows confirm April 30; for state special calls recompute due date = bulletin issue date + the stated response window.

Recompute the four internal milestones (extract at due minus 30 days, validation at due minus 10 business days, sign-off at due minus 5, submit at due minus 2) and confirm none falls before the valuation date.
Any date difference of one day or more is an exception.
testing.done: every sampled due date and milestone set is recomputed and agrees, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace each sampled calendar row to its actual submission outcome
actions: For each sampled row locate the submission confirmation receipt from the agent portal or department and read its transmission timestamp.
Compare the transmission timestamp to the recorded regulatory due date and mark on-time, late or not submitted.
For rows marked submitted in the register with no retrievable receipt, treat the status as unsupported and log it.
Confirm any extension claimed on the row is backed by written agent or department correspondence dated before the due date.
testing.done: every sampled row is traced to a dated receipt or listed as unsupported/late, with extensions evidenced.

testing.step: Test the ad-hoc intake path end to end
actions: Pull every message in the Stat Reporting mailbox folder for the quarter matching 'data call', 'statistical plan' or 'reporting requirement'.
Confirm each has a dated intake form and either a register row created within 5 business days or a recorded not-applicable reason with an author.
Measure receipt-to-register-row days for each and list any over 5 business days.
Confirm calls with a response window under 30 days were notified to the Regulatory Reporting Manager the same day.
testing.done: every inbound call is accounted for with an intake form and a measured, within-SLA registration or a reasoned exclusion.

testing.step: Prove the reminder and escalation configuration actually fires
actions: Export the notification configuration and the notification send log for the quarter from the Statistical Reporting register.
For 10 sampled rows confirm T-60, T-30, T-10 and T-2 alerts were generated and delivered to the named data owner and manager.
Confirm the T-10 auto-escalation fired for every row that was still 'Not started' at that point.
Missing sends, or sends to a departed employee's address, are exceptions.
testing.done: the send log evidences all four alerts and every due auto-escalation for the sampled rows, to current addressees.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception stating jurisdiction, agent, call name, due date, what was missed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: circular not triaged, agent designation stale, valuation date misread, owner unassigned, notification misrouted.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any missed statistical call open a late-reporting assessment with the Regulatory Affairs Manager.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the calendar completeness test
actions: Compute the completeness exception rate and the on-time submission rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance completeness threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who does not maintain the calendar, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
File the workpaper under REG-007-C01 and report results and any missed statistical call to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns extraction and validation of statistical records for every data call; certifies the file to the Regulatory Reporting Manager before it leaves the building

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — the data element list is traced to the Alabama statistical plan record layout via the NCCI Statistical Plan and the ISO Commercial Statistical Plan editions in force at the valuation date, with Arizona, California and Connecticut plan variances noted on the mapping

In-scope processes.value: Statistical record build for Alternative Risk and all other lines — premium and exposure extraction from policy administration, loss and reserve extraction from claims, premium audit adjustment capture, code mapping to the stat plan layout, edit-package validation and reconciliation to the general ledger

In-scope systems.value: Policy administration and claims data landed in the warehouse statistical staging layer, transformed to the ISO/NCCI record layouts and validated before hand-off to submission

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statistical Data Extraction and Validation Procedure — valuation-date freeze, layout version control, code mapping tables, three validation tiers (format, cross-field, reasonability), GL reconciliation and data-owner attestation

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Data Officer; re-approved on every stat plan edition change and at least annually

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Validation must complete 10 business days before each call's due date — for NCCI unit statistical reports that means valuation at 18 months from policy effective date with validation closed inside the 20-day reporting window, and for annual financial calls validation closed by mid-March against the March 31 due date

Deadline reminders configured.value: Pipeline alerts on the orchestrator at extract date (due minus 30 days) and validation-complete date (due minus 10 business days), plus a failed-run alert to the Data Quality Analyst on duty within 15 minutes

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Validation report, edit-package version, code mapping version, GL reconciliation and data-owner attestations retained 7 years from the reporting period alongside the submitted file

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every failed validation rule is logged with record count, sample keys, disposition (corrected at source / corrected in mapping / accepted with rationale) and the approver

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off any statistical file released with accepted (uncorrected) validation failures, and every mapping change made to clear an edit

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All statistical records built for calls with a valuation date in the quarter — premium/exposure and loss records by writing company, state and line, plus the source policy and claim populations they were drawn from

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero critical (fatal) edits outstanding at release; premium reconciled to the general ledger within 0.5% by state and line with every difference explained; paid and incurred losses reconciled to the reserving extract within 0.5%; any unexplained difference above threshold is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per data call; validation testing runs on every file before release, and the independent test runs quarterly over that quarter's valuation dates with 100% coverage of Alabama and NCCI unit statistical files

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built or mapped any sampled statistical record set

Evidence location for test results.value: Validation workpaper per call (rule results, record counts, GL reconciliation, sampled record re-performance, exception dispositions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-007-C02

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Validation report plus record-layout mapping and GL reconciliation, producible for an ISO/NCCI data quality review or an ALDOI statistical data inquiry within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Data Quality Manager answers statistical agent data-quality queries with the validation report; Regulatory Reporting Manager owns the formal reply and Regulatory Counsel clears any restatement communicated to a department

checklist.step: Freeze the valuation date and lock the reporting scope
actions: Take the call's valuation date, reporting period, writing companies, states and lines from the Data Call Calendar row and copy them onto a new extraction request.
Confirm with the Controller that the general ledger period covering the valuation date is closed and will not be reopened.
State explicitly on the request whether the call is on a policy-year, accident-year or calendar-year basis, because the extract joins differ for each.
Send the extraction request to the Data Engineer and the named data owners, and record the request date on the calendar row.
checklist.done: an extraction request exists naming valuation date, basis, companies, states and lines against a closed GL period.

checklist.step: Pin the record layout and edit package versions the file must satisfy
actions: Download the record layout in force at the valuation date — the NCCI WCSTAT/WCPOLS record layouts and edit matrix from the NCCI Data Reporting section, or the ISO Commercial Statistical Plan record specification from the Verisk statistical reporting site.
Record the layout edition and effective date on the validation workpaper and diff it against the layout version currently coded in the transformation.
Where fields, code values or edits changed, list each change and raise a change request to the ETL Developer with the required-by date set to the extract milestone.
For Alabama confirm any state-specific field or exception noted in the statistical plan is reflected, and repeat for Arizona, California and Connecticut.
checklist.done: the layout and edit-package editions are pinned on the workpaper and any delta is raised as a dated change request.

checklist.step: Extract premium and exposure records from the policy administration platform
actions: Run the statistical extract job against the policy administration platform as of the frozen valuation date, restricted to the requested companies, states and lines.

Pull the fields the layout requires: policy number, effective and expiration dates, writing company/carrier code, state code, class code, exposure base and amount, territory, coverage code, deductible, written premium and transaction effective date.
Include endorsements, cancellations and reinstatements as their own transaction records with the correct transaction codes, not netted into the original.
For Alternative Risk business pull the large deductible, retro and self-insured-group indicators and the deductible amount so those records can be reported separately.
Land the output in the warehouse statistical staging layer with the run id, valuation date and record count in the load control table.
checklist.done: premium and exposure records for the full scope are staged with transaction-level detail and a logged run id and count.

checklist.step: Extract loss, reserve and claim detail records from the claims platform
actions: Run the loss extract as of the same valuation date, joined to the policy records on policy number and effective date so orphan claims are visible.

Pull claim number, accident/loss date, report date, claim status, cause of loss, injury/nature of injury and body part codes, part of body and event codes for workers compensation, paid indemnity, paid medical, paid expense, case reserves and recoveries.
Include claims closed without payment and reopened claims with the correct status codes — omitting them distorts frequency in the stat plan.
Ask the Reserving Analyst for the reserve balances at the same valuation date so case reserves in the extract can be tied out later.
Land the loss records in the same staging layer with run id and count.
checklist.done: loss records for the scope are staged at the same valuation date, joined to policies, with reserve balances supplied by Reserving.

checklist.step: Capture premium audit and retrospective adjustments into the exposure
actions: List every completed premium audit and retrospective adjustment with an effective date on or before the valuation date for policies in scope.
Confirm the audited exposure and audited premium have been posted back to the policy administration platform, and list any audit completed but unposted.
For Alternative Risk large deductible and retro policies, confirm the exposure reported is the standard/manual basis the stat plan requires, not the discounted net premium.
Hand the unposted list to the Policy Administration Analyst with a posting deadline set before the extract milestone, and re-run the affected records after posting.
checklist.done: all audits effective by the valuation date are posted, or the unposted list is closed before the extract is finalised.

checklist.step: Map source values to the statistical plan code sets
actions: Open the reference data platform and load the current code sets: NCCI class codes and state exception classes, ISO statistical class and coverage codes, ANSI/FIPS state codes, territory codes and cause-of-loss codes.
Map every distinct source value in the staged extract to a plan code and list any source value with no mapping as an unmapped exception.
Apply state exception mappings where the plan differs by jurisdiction — Alabama, Arizona, California and Connecticut each carry their own class or territory exceptions.
Version the mapping table with an effective date and record the version id on the validation workpaper.
Route new or changed mappings to the Data Governance Lead for approval before they are used in a live file.
checklist.done: no source value is unmapped, state exceptions are applied, and the mapping version is approved and recorded.

checklist.step: Run tier-1 format and structural validation against the layout
actions: Run the format rule set: record length, field positions, numeric/alphanumeric type, sign handling, date format, mandatory-field presence and valid code-set membership for every coded field.
Check header and trailer records carry the correct carrier code, reporting period and record counts.
Output a rule-by-rule result table showing rule id, severity (fatal/critical/warning), failed record count and 10 sample record keys per rule.
Stop the pipeline on any fatal rule failure rather than passing the file downstream.
checklist.done: a rule-by-rule tier-1 result table exists and no fatal format failure remains open.

checklist.step: Run tier-2 cross-field and relational edits
actions: Run the relational edits the plan requires: loss date within the policy term, expiration after effective, class code valid for the state and line, exposure present where premium is non-zero, paid amounts not exceeding incurred, reserve non-negative unless a recovery code is present.
Check every loss record joins to a premium record for the same policy, company and state, and list orphans both ways.
Check transaction sequences reconcile — original plus endorsements minus cancellations equals the in-force premium on the policy.
Record each failure with its rule id, count and sample keys on the validation workpaper.
checklist.done: all cross-field and relational edits are executed with counts and sample keys, and orphan records are listed both directions.

checklist.step: Reconcile statistical premium to the general ledger by state and line
actions: Pull written and earned premium by writing company, state and line from the general ledger for the reporting period at the frozen valuation date.
Summarise the statistical file to the same grain and place the two side by side in a reconciliation sheet.
Explain every difference by named reconciling item — non-statistical lines, assumed reinsurance, policy fees, installment charges, timing of endorsements — and quantify each.
Flag any unexplained difference above 0.5% of the GL amount for that state and line as a blocking exception.
Have the Statutory Reporting Manager review the reconciliation against the Annual Statement state page for the same period.
checklist.done: premium ties to the GL by state and line within 0.5% with every reconciling item named and quantified.

checklist.step: Reconcile statistical losses to the reserving and Annual Statement basis
actions: Summarise paid, case reserve and incurred losses from the statistical file by company, state, line and accident/policy year.
Compare to the reserving system triangles at the same valuation date and to the Schedule P basis where the call is annual.
Explain differences by named item — bulk/IBNR excluded from stat reporting, allocated versus unallocated expense treatment, salvage and subrogation netting, reinsurance gross versus net basis.
Flag unexplained differences above 0.5% as blocking and hand them back to the Data Engineer with the affected claim keys.
checklist.done: paid, case and incurred losses tie to the reserving extract within 0.5% with differences named and quantified.

checklist.step: Run tier-3 reasonability and prior-period comparison
actions: Build the comparison view: current file versus the same call one period back, by state, line and class code, showing record counts, exposure, premium and incurred loss.
Flag any state/line cell moving more than 15% period on period, any class code appearing or disappearing entirely, and any average premium or average claim size outside the prior period's range.
Compute the loss ratio by state and line and flag values below 5% or above 200% for investigation.
For each flag write a one-line business explanation with the name of the person who supplied it, or send it back for correction.
checklist.done: every reasonability flag carries a named business explanation or a correction, none is left unexplained.

checklist.step: Disposition every open validation failure before release
actions: Work the open failure list rule by rule and set a disposition on each: corrected at source system, corrected via approved mapping change, or accepted with written rationale.
Corrections at source go to the Policy Administration Analyst or Claims Analyst with the record keys and a same-cycle due date, then the extract is re-run rather than patched.
Never edit the output file by hand — a change that cannot be reproduced by re-running the pipeline is itself an exception.
Route every 'accepted' disposition to the Chief Data Officer for written sign-off before release.
checklist.done: no failure is left undispositioned, corrections were made at source and re-extracted, and accepted items carry CDO sign-off.

checklist.step: Collect data-owner attestations for each source domain
actions: Send each named data owner the summary for their domain: record counts, key totals and the open items in their area.
Require a written attestation that the data is complete and accurate as of the valuation date for the stated scope.
Chase any attestation outstanding at validation-complete minus 2 business days and escalate to the Data Quality Manager.
Attach the attestations to the validation workpaper with names and dates.
checklist.done: a dated written attestation exists for premium, loss, audit and reserve data from each named owner.

checklist.step: Produce the validation report and release the file to submission
actions: Assemble the validation report: call identity and valuation date, layout and edit-package versions, mapping version, record counts by type, tier-1/2/3 rule results, GL and reserving reconciliations, dispositions and attestations.
State the release decision explicitly with your name and date, and list any accepted failure with its CDO sign-off reference.
Hand the released file and the validation report to the Regulatory Reporting Manager and update the Data Call Calendar row to 'Validated — ready to submit'.
File the report in the compliance evidence repository under REG-007-C02 with a 7-year retention label.
checklist.done: a signed validation report accompanies the released file and the calendar row shows 'Validated — ready to submit'.

checklist.step: Feed recurring failures back into the pipeline and the source systems
actions: Take the top failing rules by record count from the last three cycles and identify which are mapping defects, which are source-capture defects and which are stale layout coding.
Raise a change request for each with the fix owner and target cycle, and add a pipeline pre-check so the failure surfaces at extract rather than at validation.
Add or tighten the rule in the quality tool where a defect got through undetected.
Report the reduction in failed record count cycle over cycle to the Data Quality Manager.
checklist.done: each recurring failure has a change request, an owner and a target cycle, with a measured cycle-over-cycle reduction.

testing.step: Rebuild the record population from source and reconcile it to the submitted file
actions: For each call with a valuation date in the quarter, independently count in-force and transacted policies and open/closed claims from the policy administration and claims platforms as of that valuation date.
Compare to the record counts in the submitted statistical file by company, state and line.
List any count difference and require a named reconciling item before it is accepted.
Sign the population extract as complete and reconciled before sampling.
testing.done: the file record counts reconcile to independently counted source populations, with every difference named.

testing.step: Verify the layout and edit-package version used was the one in force
actions: Retrieve the NCCI record layout and edit matrix, and the ISO statistical plan record specification, as they stood at the valuation date.
Compare edition and effective date to the versions recorded on the validation workpaper and coded in the transformation.
Confirm any layout change issued between the prior cycle and this one was implemented, using the change request reference.
A file built on a superseded layout is an exception regardless of whether the agent accepted it.
testing.done: the layout and edit-package editions used are proven to be those in force at the valuation date.

testing.step: Draw a documented record-level sample
actions: Take 40 premium/exposure records and 40 loss records at random using a recorded seed, stratified so Alabama and every NCCI state is represented.
Add 100% of records that were dispositioned 'accepted with rationale' and 100% of Alternative Risk large deductible records.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Retrieve the source policy and claim keys for every sampled record.
testing.done: a reproducible, stratified sample is drawn with source keys retrieved for every selected record.

testing.step: Re-perform the code mapping for each sampled record against the source system
actions: Open each sampled policy in the policy administration platform and read the underlying class, territory, coverage, deductible, exposure base and premium from the policy screens.
Independently derive the plan code for each field from the current NCCI or ISO code set before looking at the file value.
Compare to the reported code and treat a difference in any coded field as an exception, including a correct code carried on a stale mapping version.
Capture the policy screen and the code-set page you relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent code derivation, a comparison result and captured source screens.

testing.step: Re-perform the loss record derivation against the claim file
actions: Open each sampled claim and read loss date, report date, status, cause of loss and injury coding, paid indemnity, paid medical, paid expense and case reserve as of the valuation date using the financial history screen.
Compare each amount and code to the reported statistical record and check the loss date falls inside the policy term.
Confirm claims closed without payment and reopened claims carry the correct status code in the file.
Any amount difference, or a claim present in the system but absent from the file, is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled loss record ties to the claim file at the valuation date on amounts, codes and status.

testing.step: Recompute the general ledger and reserving reconciliations
actions: Independently pull written and earned premium by company, state and line from the general ledger for the reporting period and re-foot the file summary to the same grain.
Recompute the variance percentage per cell and compare to the 0.5% threshold.
Test each named reconciling item to supporting evidence — do not accept 'timing' or 'system difference' without a quantified schedule.
Repeat for paid, case and incurred losses against the reserving extract.
testing.done: both reconciliations are independently recomputed, within threshold, and every reconciling item is evidenced.

testing.step: Test that the validation rule set actually covers the plan's edits
actions: List every edit in the agent's published edit matrix and map it to a rule id in the quality tool.
List plan edits with no corresponding internal rule as coverage gaps and rank them by the agent's severity.
Inject 10 deliberately invalid records covering the highest-severity edits into a test run and confirm each is caught with the right severity.
An edit the agent enforces but the internal rule set does not test is an exception even if no live record failed it.
testing.done: every published plan edit maps to an internal rule, and injected invalid records are caught at the correct severity.

testing.step: Challenge every accepted (uncorrected) validation failure
actions: Pull each failure dispositioned 'accepted with rationale' and read the written rationale and the record counts behind it.
Confirm the Chief Data Officer sign-off exists, names the rule, and is dated before the file release.
Assess whether the acceptance would survive an agent data-quality review or an ALDOI inquiry, and challenge any rationale that amounts to 'not material'.
Confirm the same rule was not accepted in the two prior cycles without a remediation plan.
testing.done: every accepted failure has a dated CDO sign-off, a defensible rationale and no unremediated repeat across cycles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the call, valuation date, record keys, the field or rule involved and the reporting impact.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: stale layout, unmapped source value, unposted premium audit, source capture defect, reconciliation not investigated, hand edit of output.
Set an owner and a remediation cycle, and where records were already submitted, open a correction-record action under REG-007-C04.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation cycle and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the validation test
actions: Compute the record-level error rate by field group and the reconciliation variance by state and line, and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Data Governance Lead, who built none of the sampled record sets, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
File under REG-007-C02 and report error rates and any restatement to the Compliance Committee and the Chief Data Officer.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, error rate, variance summary and reporting date is filed in the repository.

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — submission channel and format confirmed against the Alabama statistical plan and the ALDOI statistical agent designation, plus the agent's current data reporting circular; Arizona, California and Connecticut plans re-read where they take data outside the common agent channel

In-scope processes.value: Statistical file transmission for Alternative Risk and all other lines — file generation in the plan format, portal or SFTP transmission to ISO/Verisk, NCCI Data Transfer or AIPSO, MCAS filing in NAIC iSite+, and department-portal responses to state special calls across 51 jurisdictions

In-scope systems.value: Submission packages assembled and status-tracked against the Data Call Calendar row; confirmation receipts attached to the row on transmission

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statistical Submission Procedure — release gate on the validation sign-off, format generation and control totals, entitlement check, transmission, receipt capture, accepted-count verification and status update

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved annually and on any agent change to transmission channel, file naming or acknowledgement format

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per data call — transmit no later than due date minus 2 business days: NCCI policy data within 30 days of policy effective date, NCCI unit statistical inside the 20-day window at 18 months, NCCI financial calls by March 31/April 1, ISO stat submissions on the published monthly cut-off, NAIC MCAS by April 30, and the stated response date on each state special call

Deadline reminders configured.value: Calendar alerts at T-10, T-5 and T-2 business days on the submission task, plus a same-day alert to the Regulatory Reporting Manager if the row is not in status 'Submitted' by 12:00 on the due date

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any transmission after the regulatory due date, or any submission without a retrievable confirmation receipt, is logged as a late/unevidenced filing exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late statistical submission and any decision to submit partial data, before the file is transmitted where possible

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All statistical calls with a regulatory due date in the quarter across the 51 jurisdictions and every designated agent, taken from the Data Call Calendar and cross-checked to agent portal submission histories

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% on-time transmission — any file transmitted after its due date is a fail; any submitted row without a timestamped confirmation receipt is a fail; any accepted record count differing from the submitted count without an explanation is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per data call; the submission test runs quarterly over that quarter's due dates with 100% coverage of NCCI unit statistical and financial calls, MCAS and all Alabama submissions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have transmitted any sampled file or hold the portal entitlement used

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly submission timeliness workpaper (calendar extract, portal submission history, receipt evidence, timeliness computation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-007-C03

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-call submission package — transmitted file, control totals, agent confirmation receipt and acceptance report — producible for an ALDOI statistical data inquiry or an agent audit within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager responds to agent submission queries; Regulatory Affairs Manager owns department correspondence on missed or late statistical calls and Regulatory Counsel clears any written admission of lateness

checklist.step: Confirm the validation release gate before any file is generated
actions: Open the Data Call Calendar row and confirm status is 'Validated — ready to submit' with the signed validation report attached.
Read the validation report's release decision and note any accepted failure that the agent may query on receipt.
Where the row is not validated, stop and escalate to the Data Quality Manager rather than transmitting an unvalidated file.
Record the gate check with your name and timestamp on the calendar row.
checklist.done: the row carries a signed validation report and a timestamped gate check before file generation starts.

checklist.step: Generate the transmission file in the exact format the agent requires
actions: Run the file-generation job for the released record set in the required format — fixed-width WCPOLS/WCSTAT for NCCI, the ISO statistical plan flat-file layout for Verisk, the AIPSO plan layout for residual market, or the NAIC MCAS Excel template for MCAS.
Apply the agent's file naming convention exactly, including carrier code, reporting period and sequence number — a wrongly named file is rejected at the gateway before any edit runs.
Write the header and trailer records with carrier code, reporting period, valuation date and record counts by record type.
Confirm character encoding, record length and line terminators match the specification, and that the file is not zipped unless the agent requires it.
Produce a control-total sheet showing record counts, total premium, total exposure, total paid and total incurred.
checklist.done: the file matches the agent's layout, naming and encoding rules and is accompanied by a control-total sheet.

checklist.step: Verify portal entitlements and credentials before the transmission window
actions: At T-5 business days sign in to each destination — ncci.com Data Manager, the Verisk statistical reporting portal, AIPSO, NAIC iSite+ — and confirm the account is active and not password-expired.
Confirm the carrier codes you must submit for are all visible under your entitlement, not just the primary company.
Where multi-factor authentication is enforced, confirm the registered device is current and a backup approver has the same entitlement.
Raise an access request to the Access Management Analyst immediately for anything missing, quoting the due date.
checklist.done: every destination portal is confirmed accessible at T-5 with all carrier codes visible and a backup approver entitled.

checklist.step: Transmit the file to the designated statistical agent
actions: For NCCI, sign in to ncci.com, open Data Manager ▸ Data Transfer, select the carrier code and data type (WCPOLS, WCSTAT, financial call) and upload the file.
For ISO/Verisk, open Statistical Reporting ▸ Data Submission, select the stat plan and reporting period and upload the file, or place it on the agreed SFTP endpoint with the agreed filename.
For AIPSO, upload through the residual market reporting screen for the specific state plan.
Watch the upload through to a submitted state — do not close the browser on an in-progress upload — and record the transmission timestamp in your local time and the portal's.
Transmit no later than the due date minus 2 business days so a rejection can still be corrected in time.
checklist.done: the file reaches a submitted state in the agent portal with the transmission timestamp recorded.

checklist.step: Capture the confirmation receipt as the evidence artifact
actions: Download or screenshot the portal's confirmation, which must show the file name, carrier code, reporting period, submission reference number and timestamp.
Save the agent's acknowledgement email into the same package, and where the agent returns an acknowledgement file, save it verbatim.
Name the package REG-007-<agent>-<state or ALL>-<period>-submission and attach the transmitted file and control-total sheet to it.
File the package in the compliance evidence repository under REG-007-C03 and link it on the Data Call Calendar row — a submission with no receipt counts as unevidenced.
checklist.done: a receipt showing reference number and timestamp is filed with the transmitted file and linked on the calendar row.

checklist.step: Verify accepted record counts against submitted counts
actions: Open the agent's processing report — the NCCI Data Manager submission summary or the Verisk submission status screen — once processing completes, usually within 1 to 3 business days.
Compare accepted, rejected and pended record counts to the control-total sheet submitted with the file.
Where accepted is lower than submitted, list the rejected record keys and hand them straight to the exception process under REG-007-C04 the same day.
Record accepted counts and any variance on the calendar row so the submission is not treated as complete on transmission alone.
checklist.done: accepted, rejected and pended counts are reconciled to the control totals and any shortfall is handed to the exception process.

checklist.step: File the Market Conduct Annual Statement where the company is in scope
actions: Sign in to NAIC iSite+ and open the MCAS application for the reporting year and the required company/state/line combinations.
Upload or key the MCAS data using the current year template, completing the interrogatories as well as the numeric schedules.
Run the application's validations, clear every hard edit and document the explanation for each soft edit before submitting.
Submit by April 30 and download the submission confirmation with its filing reference for each state and line.
Attach the confirmations to the calendar rows and to the evidence package.
checklist.done: every in-scope MCAS filing is submitted by April 30 with edits cleared and a per-state confirmation captured.

checklist.step: Respond to state-specific special calls through the department's own channel
actions: Read the bulletin's response instructions and use the exact channel named — department portal, secure upload, or the email address given with the required subject line format.
Complete the department's own template unchanged; do not substitute an internal report layout or add columns the template does not have.
Include the cover letter the bulletin asks for, naming the company, NAIC code, contact name, phone and email.
Request and retain a written acknowledgement where the channel does not generate one automatically, and record the department contact and date.
checklist.done: each special call is answered on the department's own template and channel with a retained acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Settle any filing fee, assessment or invoice attached to the submission
actions: Check the agent's invoice or the department's fee schedule for the call and confirm the amount, payment method and due date.
Raise the payment in the general ledger with the call reference in the description so it can be traced back to the submission.
Confirm the payment cleared before the fee due date and attach the remittance advice to the submission package.
Escalate any disputed assessment to the Regulatory Reporting Manager rather than withholding payment past the due date.
checklist.done: any fee or assessment is paid before its due date with remittance advice attached to the submission package.

checklist.step: Update the calendar status and notify the stakeholders
actions: Set the calendar row status to 'Submitted' with the transmission timestamp, submission reference number and receipt link.
Notify the data owner, the Data Quality Manager and the Regulatory Reporting Manager that the call is submitted, quoting accepted counts once known.
Where the submission was partial or carried accepted validation failures, state that plainly in the notification rather than in a footnote.
Close the notification loop by confirming the row no longer appears in the open-obligations view.
checklist.done: the row shows 'Submitted' with timestamp, reference and receipt link, and stakeholders are notified.

checklist.step: Confirm downstream acceptance by the agent and clear pended records
actions: At 5 business days after transmission re-open the agent's submission status screen and confirm the submission has moved past processing to accepted.
Chase any submission still pending processing with the agent's data reporting contact, quoting the submission reference number.
Where the agent applies a data quality score or performance measure to the carrier, record the current score and compare it to the prior cycle.
Move rows to 'Accepted' only on the agent's own confirmation, never on assumption.
checklist.done: each submission is confirmed accepted by the agent, or chased with a dated contact record, before the row is closed.

checklist.step: Handle a missed or at-risk due date openly and in writing
actions: Where a due date will be missed, decide before the date passes between transmitting partial data with a cover note or requesting a written extension from the agent or department.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager send the extension request in writing to the named agent or department contact, stating the call, period, reason and committed date.
Sign off the decision and record it on the calendar row with the correspondence attached.
Where the date passes without submission, direct that the file is transmitted at the earliest possible moment and a late-filing notification is issued to the agent the same day.
checklist.done: every at-risk or missed date has a signed decision, written correspondence and a committed submission date on the row.

checklist.step: Protect the submission package integrity in transit and at rest
actions: Transmit only over the agent's secure portal or the agreed SFTP endpoint; never send statistical files containing claimant detail by unencrypted email.
Compute and record a hash of the transmitted file on the control-total sheet so a later retrieval can be proven identical.
Restrict the submission package folder to the regulatory reporting group and the compliance reviewers.
Where a file must be re-sent, send the identical hashed file rather than regenerating it, unless the content genuinely changed.
checklist.done: the file was sent over a secure channel, its hash is recorded, and folder access is restricted to named groups.

checklist.step: Run the month-end submission completeness sweep
actions: At each month end list every calendar row with a due date in the month and its status.
Confirm each is 'Submitted' or 'Accepted' with a receipt link, and investigate every row still open.
Cross-check the list against each agent portal's own submission history for the month so a submission made outside the process is still captured.
Report the on-time rate by agent and jurisdiction to the Head of Compliance with a one-line reason for every miss.
checklist.done: every row due in the month is closed with a receipt or explained, and the on-time rate is reported by agent and jurisdiction.

checklist.step: Archive the completed submission package
actions: Assemble the final package: transmitted file, control totals with hash, confirmation receipt, agent acceptance report, any correspondence and the fee remittance.
File it under REG-007-C03 indexed by jurisdiction, agent, call name, reporting period and submission reference number.
Apply the 7-year retention label and hand the package to Records Management for the retention controls under REG-007-C05.
Confirm the package is retrievable by searching on the submission reference number alone.
checklist.done: the complete package is filed, indexed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by submission reference number.

testing.step: Build the population of calls due in the quarter and reconcile to portal histories
actions: Extract every Data Call Calendar row with a regulatory due date inside the quarter, across 51 jurisdictions, all writing companies and all agents.
Independently export the submission history for the same period from NCCI Data Manager, the Verisk statistical reporting portal, AIPSO and NAIC iSite+.
Reconcile both ways — calendar rows with no portal submission, and portal submissions with no calendar row — and resolve every difference before sampling.
Sign the reconciled population as complete.
testing.done: the calendar population and the agent portal histories are reconciled both ways with no unexplained difference.

testing.step: Recompute on-time status for the whole population
actions: For each population row take the transmission timestamp from the confirmation receipt, not from the calendar status field.
Compute days early or late against the regulatory due date, using the agent's stated time zone and cut-off time.
Compute the on-time rate overall, by agent and by jurisdiction, and list every late row with its days late.
Confirm any row claimed as extended has written agent or department correspondence dated before the original due date.
testing.done: on-time status is recomputed from receipts for the full population with every late row and extension listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of NCCI unit statistical and financial call submissions, 100% of MCAS filings and 100% of Alabama submissions.
Take 20 further rows at random using a recorded seed across the remaining agents and jurisdictions.
Include every row identified as late or unevidenced in the on-time recomputation.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all NCCI, MCAS, Alabama and late rows plus 20 random rows is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the submission lookup in the agent portal for each sampled row
actions: Sign in to the relevant portal under read-only access and search the recorded submission reference number for the sampled row.
Confirm the submission exists for the right carrier code, data type, reporting period and valuation date.
Read the portal's own timestamp and status and compare both to the retained receipt — a receipt that does not match the portal record is an exception.
Capture the portal submission detail screen into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled submission is located in the agent portal and its portal record matches the retained receipt.

testing.step: Verify control totals travelled intact from validation to acceptance
actions: Compare the record counts and premium/loss totals on the validation report, the control-total sheet and the agent's acceptance report for each sampled row.
Recompute the file's own header and trailer counts from the retained transmitted file and compare to the control-total sheet.
Recompute the file hash and compare it to the hash recorded at transmission to prove the retained file is the one sent.
Any break in this chain of three is an exception.
testing.done: validation totals, control totals, transmitted-file counts, hash and agent acceptance agree for every sampled row.

testing.step: Re-perform the MCAS filing check in NAIC iSite+
actions: Open the NAIC MCAS application for the reporting year and list the company/state/line combinations shown as filed.
Compare to the NAIC participation requirements for the company's premium volume and lines and list any required filing that is absent.
Confirm each filing carries a submission confirmation dated on or before April 30 and that hard edits were cleared before submission.
Capture the filing status screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every required MCAS filing is evidenced as submitted by April 30 with edits cleared, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Test the entitlement and segregation around the transmission function
actions: Export the current entitlement list for NCCI Data Manager, the Verisk statistical portal, AIPSO and NAIC iSite+ from the access platform and the portals themselves.
Confirm every entitled user is a current employee in the regulatory reporting function and that leavers were removed within the joiner-mover-leaver SLA.
Confirm at least two entitled users exist per destination and that the reviewer of this test holds none of these entitlements.
List any orphan, shared or generic account as an exception.
testing.done: portal entitlements are current, dual-covered, free of shared accounts and segregated from the reviewer.

testing.step: Verify accepted-count follow-up actually happened
actions: For each sampled row read the agent's acceptance report and note accepted, rejected and pended counts.
Where accepted is below submitted, confirm a corresponding exception exists under REG-007-C04 opened within one business day of the report.
Confirm the row was only moved to 'Accepted' on the agent's own confirmation and not on transmission alone.
A closed calendar row with unresolved rejected records is an exception.
testing.done: every shortfall between submitted and accepted counts is traced to a raised exception and an open row.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with jurisdiction, agent, call, due date, transmission timestamp and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: validation ran late, entitlement lapsed, wrong file name or layout, portal outage not escalated, receipt not captured, row closed on assumption.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for any late statistical call open a late-reporting assessment with the Regulatory Affairs Manager and Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the submission timeliness test
actions: Compute the on-time rate and the evidenced-receipt rate and compare both to the 100% thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who holds no portal entitlement and transmitted none of the sampled files, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
File under REG-007-C03 and report the on-time rate and every late statistical call to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, on-time rate, receipt rate and committee reporting date is filed.
