checklist.step: Retrieve the agent's error and criticism listings on a fixed cadence
actions: Every business day open NCCI Data Manager ▸ Data Manager Dashboard and download the outstanding criticism and edit listings for each carrier code.
Open the Verisk statistical reporting portal ▸ Data Submission ▸ error listings and download the current cycle's rejected and pended record report.
Check the AIPSO residual market reporting screens and the regulatory reporting mailbox for department-issued error notices.
Save each listing raw and unedited into the exception evidence folder named <agent>-errors-<yyyy-mm-dd> before any manipulation.
Where a portal shows no new listing, record the nil check with the date so a gap in retrieval cannot be mistaken for a clean cycle.
checklist.done: every agent portal has a dated listing download or a recorded nil check for the day.

checklist.step: Load the listings into the exception register and join them to source keys
actions: Parse each listing into register rows: agent, carrier code, state, reporting period, record type, record key, edit/criticism code, agent's severity and issue date.
Join each row back to the warehouse statistical record on policy number and effective date, or claim number, to recover the source system key.
List rows that cannot be joined — usually agent-side records the company no longer holds — and treat them as their own investigation stream.
Compute the agent's stated response deadline on each row from the issue date and the circular's response window.
checklist.done: every listing row is a register entry joined to a source key with a computed response deadline, or is on the unjoinable list.

checklist.step: Classify every error by severity and by error family
actions: Set severity from the agent's own code: fatal/reject (record not accepted), critical (accepted but must be corrected), warning (informational).

Assign an error family: coding (class, territory, coverage, cause of loss), financial (premium, exposure, paid, reserve), structural (layout, sequence, duplicate), relational (loss without policy, dates out of term), or timeliness (record reported late).
Rank the register by severity then by financial magnitude of the records affected.
Flag any error touching workers compensation unit statistical data that feeds an experience rating modification, because those carry a hard rating deadline.
checklist.done: every register entry carries an agent severity, an error family, a rank and an experience-rating flag where relevant.

checklist.step: Triage each entry to an owning team within one business day
actions: Assign coding and financial premium errors to the Policy Administration Analyst, loss and reserve errors to the Claims Analyst, exposure errors to the Premium Auditor, and structural or mapping errors to the ETL Developer.
Set the correction due date at issue date plus 10 business days for fatal and critical entries, and inside the agent's response window in all cases.
Send the assignment with the record keys, the agent's edit text and a link to the raw listing — never a summary alone.
Escalate the same day where the assignee disputes ownership rather than letting the entry sit unowned.
checklist.done: every entry has an owning team, a named assignee and a correction due date set within one business day of receipt.

checklist.step: Establish the root cause before touching any data
actions: For each entry open the source record and decide whether the value is wrong at source, wrong in the mapping, or right at source and misread by a stale layout.
Where the source is wrong, identify how it got there — data entry, a defaulted field, a missing premium audit posting, an incorrect claim coding at first notice of loss.
Where the mapping is wrong, identify the mapping version and the code set edition it was built against.
Write the root cause onto the register row in one sentence naming the system and the field — 'unknown' is not a permitted value.
Where the cause is systemic, open a change request immediately rather than waiting for the correction to be filed.
checklist.done: every entry carries a one-sentence root cause naming system and field, with a change request raised for systemic causes.

checklist.step: Correct the data in the system of record, not in the extract
actions: Open each affected policy in the policy administration platform and correct the class code, territory, exposure, coverage or premium field the criticism names.
Where the correction changes premium, process it as a properly dated endorsement or correction transaction so the general ledger and the statistical record stay aligned.
Ask the Underwriting Assistant or the servicing underwriter to confirm the corrected value where underwriting judgement is involved, and record who confirmed it.
Never patch the statistical extract or the outbound file to satisfy an edit while leaving the source wrong — that guarantees the same criticism next cycle.
Record the source correction reference on the register row.
checklist.done: every premium-side correction is made and dated in the source system with a confirmation and a recorded reference.

checklist.step: Correct loss and reserve records in the claims system of record
actions: Open each criticised claim and correct the loss date, cause of loss, injury/body part coding, status, paid amounts or case reserve as the criticism requires.
Where a payment or reserve amount is wrong, route the correction through the claims financial transaction process so the general ledger moves with it.
Confirm with the handling Claims Examiner before changing any coding that drives reserving or reinsurance recovery.
Record the claim transaction reference and the date on the register row.
checklist.done: every loss-side correction is posted in the claims platform through a proper transaction with a recorded reference.

checklist.step: Rebuild the corrected statistical records and re-run the edits locally
actions: Re-extract the corrected policies and claims at the same valuation date as the original submission — not at today's date.
Apply the correct correction transaction coding the plan requires so the agent replaces rather than duplicates the record.
Run the full tier-1 and tier-2 edit set over the correction file before it leaves the warehouse, and confirm the specific criticised edit now passes.
Confirm no new edit failure was introduced by the correction, and hold the file if one was.
Produce a control-total sheet for the correction file listing record counts and the register entries it clears.
checklist.done: a correction file exists at the original valuation date, passes the criticised edit and introduces no new failure.

checklist.step: Resubmit the correction records to the agent
actions: Upload the correction file through the same channel as the original — NCCI Data Manager ▸ Data Transfer for the carrier code and data type, or the Verisk Data Submission screen for the stat plan and period.
Where the agent's process requires a criticism response rather than a record resubmission, answer inside the portal's criticism response screen quoting the criticism number.
Capture the resubmission confirmation with its reference number and timestamp and attach it to every register entry the file clears.
Resubmit inside the agent's response window and, for experience-rating-driving records, before the rating effective date.
checklist.done: the correction file or criticism response is transmitted inside the response window with a captured confirmation reference.

checklist.step: Confirm the agent has actually closed each criticism
actions: Two to five business days after resubmission re-open the agent's criticism listing and confirm the entry no longer appears as outstanding.
Where the entry persists, read the agent's new edit text — a repeat rejection means the correction was wrong, not that the agent is slow.
Record the agent's closure date on the register row and attach the listing that evidences closure.
Close register entries only on the agent's own listing, never on internal resubmission alone.
checklist.done: each register entry carries an agent-evidenced closure date and repeat rejections are reopened rather than closed.

checklist.step: Manage penalty, fine and data quality score exposure
actions: Track the agent's carrier data quality score or performance measure each cycle and compare it to the agent's published threshold.
Where an agent or department proposes a fine or assessment for late or erroneous statistical data, quantify the exposure and notify the Head of Compliance and Finance the same week.
Where the company disputes the assessment, prepare the factual response with the submission receipts and register evidence and have Regulatory Counsel clear it before sending.
Record every assessment, dispute and outcome on the register so repeat exposure is visible.
checklist.done: the data quality score is tracked each cycle and every proposed fine has a quantified exposure and a cleared response.

checklist.step: Fix the recurring cause, not just the record
actions: Group the quarter's register entries by root cause and rank the top five by record count and by financial magnitude.
For each, raise a change request naming the fix — mapping table update, source system field validation, layout version upgrade, or a new pre-submission edit — with an owner and a target cycle.
Add the corresponding rule to the pre-submission edit set so the same error is caught before transmission next cycle.
Measure and report the change in that error family's volume in the following cycle.
checklist.done: the top five recurring causes each have a change request, an owner, a new pre-submission edit and a measured next-cycle volume.

checklist.step: Report the open criticism aging weekly
actions: Publish a weekly aging view of the register: open entries by agent, severity, owning team and days open, with buckets at 0-5, 6-10, 11-30 and over 30 days.
Flag every fatal or critical entry over 10 business days and every entry past the agent's response window.
Send the view to the owning team managers and the Regulatory Reporting Manager with a named action for each flagged entry.
Track week-on-week movement so a backlog that is merely being re-aged is visible.
checklist.done: a weekly aging view is published with flagged breaches, named actions and week-on-week movement.

checklist.step: Escalate aged and repeat criticisms
actions: Escalate to the Head of Compliance any fatal or critical entry open beyond 10 business days, any entry past the agent's response window, and any record rejected twice.
State on the escalation the jurisdiction, agent, criticism code, records affected, the blocker and the regulatory consequence including experience rating impact.
Agree a recovery plan with a named owner and a date, and record it on the register row.
Report any statistical data believed to be materially misstated in a submitted file to the Regulatory Reporting Manager for a restatement decision.
checklist.done: every aged or repeat criticism has a written escalation, a named owner, a recovery date and a restatement decision where needed.

checklist.step: Close out and file the quarter's exception evidence
actions: Export the register for the quarter showing every entry with severity, root cause, correction, resubmission reference and agent closure date.
Attach the raw agent listings, correction files, resubmission receipts and closure listings.
Route the export to the Chief Data Officer for sign-off where any entry was closed without a data correction.
File under REG-007-C04 with a 7-year retention label, indexed by agent, jurisdiction and criticism code.
checklist.done: the quarter's register export and supporting listings are signed where required, filed and indexed for 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of agent criticisms independently of the internal register
actions: Download directly from NCCI Data Manager, the Verisk statistical reporting portal and AIPSO every error listing and criticism issued in the quarter for each carrier code.
Add department-issued error notices retrieved from the regulatory reporting mailbox for the same period.
Build a single population list with agent, carrier code, state, period, criticism code, severity and issue date.
Sign the population as complete before comparing it to anything internal.
testing.done: an agent-sourced criticism population for the quarter exists and is signed complete before internal comparison.

testing.step: Reconcile the agent population to the internal exception register
actions: Match each agent criticism to a register entry on agent + carrier code + period + criticism code + record key.
List agent criticisms with no register entry as retrieval-completeness exceptions — these are the dangerous ones because nobody was working them.
List register entries with no agent criticism as over-recording observations.
Reconcile counts by agent and severity and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: every agent criticism is matched to a register entry or listed as a retrieval-completeness exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of fatal and critical entries, 100% of Alabama entries and 100% of entries affecting workers compensation experience rating.
Take 25 further entries at random using a recorded seed across the remaining severities and agents.
Include every entry that was rejected on resubmission and every entry closed without a data correction.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all critical, Alabama, experience-rating, repeat-reject and no-correction entries is documented.

testing.step: Recompute triage, correction and response-window timing
actions: For each sampled entry compute issue date to triage date, issue date to resubmission date, and issue date to agent closure date in business days.
Compare against the 1-business-day triage SLA, the 10-business-day correction SLA and the agent's stated response window taken from the current circular.
Recompute the response window from the circular rather than accepting the register's stored deadline.
List every breach with its days over and the owning team.
testing.done: triage, correction and closure timings are recomputed against SLAs and circular windows, with breaches listed by owner.

testing.step: Re-perform the closure check in the agent portal
actions: For each sampled entry search the criticism number in the agent's portal and read its current status.
Confirm entries marked closed internally are genuinely absent from the agent's outstanding listing.
Where an entry remains outstanding at the agent but closed internally, treat it as a false-closure exception and quantify how long it has been misreported.
Capture the portal criticism status screen into the workpaper with its retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled internal closure is confirmed against the agent portal, with false closures quantified.

testing.step: Prove the correction landed in the system of record, not just in the file
actions: For sampled premium-side entries open the policy in the policy administration platform and confirm the corrected class, territory, exposure or premium value is present with a transaction date.
For sampled loss-side entries open the claim in the claims platform and confirm the corrected code, payment or reserve is posted through a financial transaction.
Where the value is right in the resubmitted file but still wrong at source, log a source-not-corrected exception — the criticism will recur.
Capture the source screen for each sampled entry.
testing.done: each sampled correction is evidenced in the source system, and file-only corrections are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Test the quality of the recorded root causes
actions: Read the root cause recorded on each sampled entry and judge whether it names a system and a field.
Reject generic causes — 'data error', 'system issue', 'human error' — as unusable and log them as root-cause quality exceptions.
Re-derive the root cause independently for 10 entries from the source record and the mapping version and compare.
Confirm entries sharing a cause are grouped rather than each carrying a bespoke narrative.
testing.done: every sampled root cause names a system and field, ten are independently re-derived, and generic causes are logged.

testing.step: Test whether recurring causes were actually remediated
actions: Take the top five root causes from each of the three prior quarters and count their entries in the current quarter.
Confirm each has a change request with an owner and a delivered or in-flight fix, and read the delivery evidence.
Confirm the corresponding pre-submission edit was added to the internal rule set and test one injected record against it.
A cause still in the top five after three quarters with no delivered fix is a fail regardless of individual entry closures.
testing.done: each recurring cause has a change request, delivery evidence and a working pre-submission edit, or is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception stating agent, jurisdiction, criticism code, record keys, days breached and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: listing not retrieved, entry not triaged, corrected in file only, closed without agent evidence, recurring cause unremediated.
Set an owner and remediation date, and where a criticism affected an experience rating modification, notify the Regulatory Affairs Manager for department follow-up.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the criticism resolution test
actions: Compute the within-SLA resolution rate, the false-closure rate and the repeat-rejection rate and compare to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who corrected and closed none of the sampled entries, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
File under REG-007-C04 and report the aging profile, any agent data quality score movement and any fine exposure to the Compliance Committee.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, resolution rate, false-closure rate and committee reporting date is filed.

In-scope systems.value: REG-007 archive tree indexed by jurisdiction, agent, call name, reporting period and submission reference, with retention labels, legal hold and immutability applied

Compliance procedure documented.value: Statistical Records Retention Procedure — defined record set per submission, retention clock start at reporting period end, indexing metadata, immutability and hashing, legal hold, retrieval SLA and approved disposition

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — each submission package must be archived within 5 business days of the agent's acceptance; retention runs 7 years from the end of the reporting period (longer where a jurisdiction's statistical plan or an open examination requires it); quarterly completeness sweeps and an annual retrieval drill

checklist.step: Define the record set that constitutes a complete statistical submission package
actions: Publish the mandatory component list: transmitted file, control-total sheet with hash, agent confirmation receipt, agent acceptance report, signed validation report, source extract manifest with run ids, mapping and layout versions, criticism register entries and any department correspondence.
State that a package missing any component is incomplete and must be raised as an exception rather than filed as-is.
Agree the list with the Regulatory Reporting Manager, the Data Quality Manager and Regulatory Counsel and record their acceptance.
Publish the list in the procedure and on the archive tree's landing page so submitters see it at filing time.
checklist.done: a published, jointly accepted component list defines completeness and is visible at the point of filing.

checklist.step: Set the retention period from the longest applicable jurisdiction requirement
actions: Build a retention matrix listing each of the 51 jurisdictions with its statistical record retention period from the state's statistical plan, insurance code or examination regulation.
Record the Alabama period against the representative row and check Arizona, California and Connecticut, since their periods differ.
Set the archive retention rule to the longest applicable period, and never shorter than 7 years from the end of the reporting period.
Extend the clock where the record supports workers compensation unit statistical data feeding experience ratings, which stay relevant across multiple rating cycles.
Have General Counsel confirm the matrix in writing and re-confirm it annually.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed retention matrix exists per jurisdiction and the archive rule uses the longest applicable period.

checklist.step: Ingest each submission package within 5 business days of acceptance
actions: Monitor the Data Call Calendar for rows moving to 'Accepted' and open an ingestion task for each.
Collect the components from the Regulatory Reporting Analyst and the Data Quality Manager and check them against the mandatory component list before accepting the package.
Create the package folder under REG-007-C05 ▸ <year> ▸ <agent> ▸ <jurisdiction> ▸ <call>-<period> and load the components.
Reject incomplete hand-offs back to the submitter with the missing component named, and raise an exception if it is not supplied within 5 further business days.
checklist.done: every accepted submission has a complete package ingested within 5 business days, or a raised exception naming the gap.

checklist.step: Apply the indexing metadata that makes the archive searchable
actions: Tag every package with jurisdiction, writing company and NAIC code, designated agent, stat plan name and edition, call name, reporting period, valuation date, due date, submission timestamp and submission reference number.
Add the line of business tag including Alternative Risk so line-specific examination requests can be answered without opening packages.
Confirm the repository's search returns the package on the submission reference number alone and on jurisdiction plus period.
Fix any package whose metadata is incomplete before it is marked ingested.
checklist.done: every package carries the full metadata set and is retrievable by submission reference and by jurisdiction plus period.

checklist.step: Apply immutability and integrity controls to the archived files
actions: Apply the repository's write-once retention lock to each package so files cannot be altered or deleted before the retention date.
Store the hash captured at transmission alongside the archived file and re-verify it on ingestion, recording pass or fail.
Restrict delete rights to the Records Manager role alone, with any deletion requiring a second approver.
Where a corrected resubmission exists, archive it as a new version linked to the original rather than overwriting it.
checklist.done: every package is write-once locked, its hash verified at ingestion, and resubmissions are versioned rather than overwritten.

checklist.step: Retain the source extracts and reconciliations behind each submission
actions: Snapshot the statistical staging tables for each submitted call at its valuation date and register the snapshot id in the package manifest.
Retain the general ledger and reserving reconciliation workbooks that supported the submission alongside the snapshot.
Confirm the snapshot can be re-queried to reproduce the submitted record counts and totals, and record the verification date.
Apply the same retention period to the snapshot as to the package so the detail does not expire before the file it supports.
checklist.done: a verifiable source snapshot and its reconciliations are retained under the same retention period as the submission.

checklist.step: Retain agent and department correspondence with the package
actions: Export from the regulatory reporting mailbox every message relating to the call — extension requests, criticism correspondence, data quality queries, fee assessments and department notices.
Save each as a dated file into the package correspondence folder rather than leaving it in a personal mailbox.
Name each file <yyyy-mm-dd>-<agent or department>-<subject> so the thread reads chronologically.
Confirm no correspondence relating to the call remains only in an individual's mailbox.
checklist.done: all call correspondence is exported into the package correspondence folder and none remains only in a personal mailbox.

checklist.step: Configure legal hold so an examination freezes disposition
actions: Agree with General Counsel the triggers that place a hold: an ALDOI or other department examination notice, an agent audit, a market conduct exam, litigation or a subpoena.
Configure the repository hold to apply by jurisdiction and period so a state examination sweeps every relevant package in one action.
Test that a held package cannot be disposed of even when its retention date passes.
Record every active hold with its trigger, scope, owner and start date, and review the register monthly.
checklist.done: holds apply by jurisdiction and period, block disposition past retention date, and are recorded and reviewed monthly.

checklist.step: Control access to the archive on least privilege
actions: Define the access groups: regulatory reporting write, compliance and audit read, records management admin with delete.
Review group membership quarterly against current employment and role, and remove leavers within the joiner-mover-leaver SLA.
Confirm no individual holds both submission-authoring and archive-delete rights.
Enable and retain the repository audit log of reads, writes and deletions for the same retention period as the records.
checklist.done: access is least-privilege, reviewed quarterly, free of author-plus-delete combinations, with an audited access log retained.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly archive completeness sweep
actions: Export the list of submissions marked accepted in the quarter from the Data Call Calendar and the archive inventory for the same period.
Match one to one and list accepted submissions with no package, and packages missing a mandatory component.
Chase each gap with the named submitter with a 5-business-day close date and escalate anything still open after that.
Publish the completeness rate by agent and jurisdiction to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the quarter's accepted submissions and archive inventory are matched one to one with every gap chased and reported.

checklist.step: Run the annual retrieval drill against a simulated examination request
actions: Have the Compliance Manager issue a simulated ALDOI request naming a jurisdiction, line and reporting period without prior warning.
Retrieve every matching package complete with file, receipt, acceptance report and validation report and record the elapsed time.
Verify each retrieved file's hash against the recorded value and confirm the package opens and reads.
Report the elapsed time against the 5-business-day target and log any package that could not be produced complete.
checklist.done: the drill produces complete, hash-verified packages within 5 business days or logs each failure with the reason.

checklist.step: Confirm backup and recoverability of the archive
actions: Confirm the REG-007 archive tree is inside the repository backup scope with the agreed recovery point and recovery time objectives.
Run a restore test on a sample of packages into an isolated environment and verify hashes after restore.
Confirm the retention lock and legal holds survive the restore rather than resetting.
Record the test date, scope and result and hand the report to the Records Manager.
checklist.done: a dated restore test proves packages recover intact with hashes, retention locks and holds preserved.

checklist.step: Review and approve disposition at end of retention
actions: Ninety days before any package reaches its retention date, review the disposition list produced by the repository.
Confirm for each package that no legal hold applies, no examination is open in that jurisdiction, and no longer jurisdiction period governs it.
Approve or defer each package in writing, recording the decision, date and reason on the disposition list.
Have Records Management execute only approved dispositions and retain the disposition certificate as a record in its own right.
checklist.done: every expiring package has a written approve-or-defer decision and any destruction has a retained disposition certificate.

checklist.step: Log archive gaps and retrieval failures as compliance exceptions
actions: Raise an issue for each missing package, missing component, failed hash verification, missed retrieval SLA or premature destruction.
State the jurisdiction, agent, call, period and the examination risk the gap creates.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and where a record cannot be reconstructed, escalate to General Counsel for an assessment of examination exposure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly sweep.
checklist.done: every archive gap or retrieval failure has an issue, an owner, a remediation date and an escalation where irrecoverable.

checklist.step: Attest annually that the statistical archive is complete and controlled
actions: Assemble the annual attestation pack: four quarterly completeness sweeps, the retrieval drill report, the restore test, the access review results and the disposition log.
State the completeness rate, the retrieval performance and any package that could not be produced.
Sign the attestation and route it to the Head of Compliance for counter-signature.
File the attestation under REG-007-C05 with the same retention period as the records it covers.
checklist.done: a signed and counter-signed annual attestation with its supporting pack is filed under the same retention period.

testing.step: Build the population of submissions that should be archived
actions: Extract every Data Call Calendar row marked accepted in the period across the 51 jurisdictions and all agents.
Independently confirm the population against the agent portal submission histories so a submission never recorded in the calendar is still captured.
Add every correction resubmission made under REG-007-C04 in the period, since each is its own archivable event.
Sign the population as complete before reconciling to the archive.
testing.done: the archivable population is built from the calendar, portal histories and correction resubmissions, and signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the archive inventory
actions: Export the REG-007 archive inventory for the period with its metadata and match to the population on submission reference number.
List submissions with no package as completeness exceptions and packages with no submission as orphan observations.
Compute the archive completeness rate overall, by agent and by jurisdiction.
Resolve every unmatched item with a named reason before sampling.
testing.done: population and archive inventory are matched on submission reference with a computed completeness rate and no unexplained gap.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Alabama packages, 100% of NCCI unit statistical and financial call packages and 100% of correction resubmission packages.
Take 25 further packages at random using a recorded seed across the remaining agents and jurisdictions.
Include every package reaching retention expiry in the period and every package under legal hold.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering Alabama, NCCI, corrections, expiring and held packages plus 25 random ones is documented.

testing.step: Test each sampled package against the mandatory component list
actions: Open each sampled package and tick off the mandatory components: transmitted file, control totals with hash, confirmation receipt, acceptance report, validation report, extract manifest, mapping and layout versions, criticism entries, correspondence.
Open each component to confirm it is the real artifact and not a placeholder or a shortcut to a personal drive.
Confirm the receipt's submission reference matches the package metadata and the transmitted file's header.
List each missing or unopenable component as an exception naming the package and component.
testing.done: each sampled package is opened, component by component, with every missing or unopenable item listed.

testing.step: Re-verify file integrity against the recorded hashes
actions: Recompute the hash of each sampled transmitted file and compare to the value recorded on the control-total sheet at transmission.
Recompute record counts and premium/loss totals from the archived file and compare to the control totals and the agent acceptance report.
Treat any hash mismatch as a potential integrity breach and escalate the same day, not as a documentation finding.
Record every verification result, pass or fail, in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled file's hash and totals are recomputed and agree, or a mismatch is escalated same-day.

testing.step: Test retrieval performance against a live unannounced request
actions: Issue an unannounced retrieval request naming a jurisdiction, agent, line and reporting period, mirroring the wording an ALDOI examination request would use.
Time the response from request to delivery of complete packages in business days.
Inspect what is delivered for completeness against the mandatory component list rather than accepting a partial set.
Compare the elapsed time to the 5-business-day target and list every package delivered late or incomplete.
testing.done: an unannounced retrieval is timed and inspected, with elapsed days measured against the 5-business-day target.

testing.step: Recompute retention expiry dates and test the retention rule
actions: For each sampled package recompute expiry = reporting period end + the longest applicable jurisdiction retention period, never less than 7 years.
Compare to the retention date the repository holds and list any package labelled short.
Cross-check the retention matrix against the current Alabama, Arizona, California and Connecticut statistical plan provisions and flag any stale period.
A package labelled shorter than its governing jurisdiction requires is an exception even if it has not yet expired.
testing.done: expiry dates are independently recomputed against a re-verified retention matrix, with every short label listed.

testing.step: Test legal hold, immutability and disposition controls
actions: Attempt, under a read-only test account, to modify and to delete a sampled package and confirm both are refused by the retention lock.
For each package under legal hold confirm the hold record names a trigger, scope, owner and start date and that disposition is blocked past the retention date.
For every package disposed of in the period, confirm a written Head of Compliance approval predates the destruction and a disposition certificate exists.
Any destruction without approval, or any destruction of a held record, is a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: modification and deletion are proven blocked, holds are complete, and every disposition has a pre-dated approval and certificate.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with jurisdiction, agent, call, period, package reference and the examination risk created.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: package never ingested, component not collected, metadata incomplete, retention period short, hold not applied, access rights excessive, retrieval SLA missed.
Set an owner and remediation date, and where a record is irrecoverable open a counsel assessment of examination exposure.
Carry every open exception into the next quarterly sweep as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: each exception has an issue, a fixed-list root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the retention test
actions: Compute the archive completeness rate, the package-component completeness rate, the hash verification pass rate and the retrieval SLA rate, and compare each to its threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with the workpaper references behind each finding.
Have the Internal Auditor, who holds no write or delete rights on the REG-007 archive, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
File under REG-007-C05 and report completeness, retrieval performance and any irrecoverable record to the Compliance Committee and General Counsel.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, the four rates and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
